objective: Execute one complete OCLOB lifecycle in which no coordinator or settlement-wide static key can open a participant order before matching, each order capability key is held as 3-of-7 verifiable shares by the MPC nodes, and only an authorized public MPC result can release enough shares for zkPI construction and canonical DeFMI settlement on a five-validator non-EVM Avalanche L1.
official_upstream_exception: MP-SPDZ compile.py is permitted only as the official compiler invoked through the Rust compiler adapter.

capability_key_protocol.creation: Each participant generates one independent random scalar per order and encrypts its fixed-size settlement capability directly under that one-order key.
capability_key_protocol.distribution: The participant creates a degree-two Shamir polynomial whose constant term is the one-order key, publishes three Feldman commitments in the signed manifest, and encrypts exactly one signed evaluation to each node's X25519 key.
capability_key_protocol.custody: Each node persists only its own encrypted order share and encrypted capability-key share; the coordinator receives neither clear shares nor a complete key.
capability_key_protocol.release: A node releases its participant-signed key share only over the settlement-role mutual-TLS channel after its durable receipt for the exact signed round authorizes that order as matched or as a published resting GTC order.
capability_key_protocol.reconstruction: The settlement process verifies three or more distinct node signatures and Feldman evaluations, reconstructs the one-order key in memory, opens the participant-signed capability, verifies DeKYX and VSS value binding, and constructs zkPI without another participant signature.
capability_key_protocol.failure_policy: Two or fewer shares fail closed; unmatched IOC orders are not released; mismatched order, round, output, node, signature, certificate, expiry, or commitment is rejected.

privacy.participant_edge: The complete SecretOrder exists only inside its participant process before verifiable sharing.
privacy.coordinator: The coordinator receives commitments, ordering certificates and signed public MPC outputs, but no complete order, complete capability key, or set of seven shares.
privacy.mpc_node: One node can open only its own order share and one capability-key evaluation. Up to two colluding nodes remain below the reconstruction threshold.
privacy.settlement: The laboratory settlement process learns the complete order only after an authorized round and a valid 3-of-7 release. It then uses that authority to reserve or settle without post-match discretion by the participant.
opened_after_match: the matched or admitted order only inside the settlement process
canonical transaction identifiers and state roots
forbidden: capability-key release before a durable authorized MPC result
private order fields or key shares in logs or public artifacts

canonical_flow: Maker and Taker independently create and distribute encrypted order shares and encrypted one-order capability-key shares
five of seven node signatures establish the Maker order position
seven malicious-shamir parties agree that the Maker rests without a fill
three or more nodes release the Maker key shares after persisting that result
the settlement process verifies Maker DeKYX evidence and finalizes the maximum inventory reservation on DeFMI
five of seven node signatures establish the Taker order position
seven malicious-shamir parties agree on the crossing Taker result
three or more nodes release both matched-order capabilities only after the agreed result
the settlement process verifies Taker DeKYX evidence and constructs threshold range-proven zkPI
Taker maximum cash reservation and all DvP legs finalize atomically
all five validators return the same state root
the identical transition is rejected as a replay
a restarted validator recovers the accepted state root

required: both participants receive signed admission receipts from all seven MPC nodes binding both encrypted payloads
two key shares cannot reconstruct the order capability and three valid shares can
participant, coordinator, and operator roles cannot request a capability-key release
settlement role cannot order, vote, execute, or query operator status
all seven nodes agree on the same program digest, artifact digest and public result for both rounds
each public release receipt binds the exact node, order, round, output digest and participant-signed key share
the Maker reservation finalizes before its order can be used by the Taker round
the Taker fills 40 lots at price 100 with no post-match signature
amount and price evidence in zkPI are threshold generated
Taker reservation and DvP finalize atomically
five validator roots agree before and after one validator restart
receipt-chain verification and replay refusal pass
reject_if: the contract SHA-256 does not match the preregistered manifest
a settlement-wide static order-decryption key exists
fewer than three distinct valid node releases open a capability
a node releases before persisting the exact authorized MPC result
an unmatched IOC order is released
any node is omitted or reports a different result
settlement values are not bound to the VSS commitments
Maker admission occurs before canonical reservation
Taker reserve exists without the corresponding DvP
the artifact exposes private order material or capability-key shares
the artifact claims independent operators, WAN evidence, HSM custody, collaborative zkPI proof generation, or account-free notes

non_claims: Seven MPC containers and five AvalancheGo validators on one host are not independent-operator or WAN evidence.
One laboratory settlement process reconstructs each one-order key after threshold release and creates zkPI; collaborative proof generation remains a production cutover.
Transition and DeFMI approval keys are deterministic laboratory keys, not HSM-backed operator custody.
Canonical DeFMI state uses commitment accounts and a reservation root rather than account-free product notes.
One functional scenario is not throughput, security-attack or economic-effect evidence.
